rationale: Methods: 6766 works with one coded passage each, all dated. Each work's rate is count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages. Works are split at 1876 (late means year >= 1876). Within each of 8 genres I took the unweighted mean of work rates for each period, then averaged the late-minus-early differences with equal genre weights. Effect = -0.0048. The 95% CI from a 2000-replicate bootstrap, resampling works within each genre-by-period cell, is [-0.032, 0.021] and includes zero. Coverage: only 1035 works fall before the cutoff, and some early genre cells are thin (other 33, romance 39). Robustness: per-genre differences are small (all within about ±0.015) except 'other' (-0.07, n=33 early). Leaving out other and collection gives +0.003. Results split by date-confidence level (high -0.009, medium +0.014, low -0.025) and by origin (UK -0.033, US +0.021) point in different directions. Decade means are flat at about 0.09-0.13 with no trend. Alternative explanations for any apparent difference: changes in genre composition over time, noisy single-passage sampling, misdating, and differences in coding confidence. The cited passages are late-period passages coded for distance/travel. They show what the construct looks like, not a trend. Conclusion: no robust historical shift.
